short: The largest empire the world had yet seen, and Greece's defining antagonist.
full:
Cyrus the Great overthrew his Median overlord Astyages in 550 BCE, the conventional starting point, then took Lydia and in 539 Babylon, where he permitted the exiled Judaeans to return home. His son Cambyses added Egypt. Darius I organised the result into some twenty satrapies with fixed tribute, a gold and silver coinage, and the Royal Road from Sardis to Susa, about 2,700 km covered by mounted relays in a week.

Two invasions of Greece failed, at Marathon in 490 and at Salamis and Plataea in 480 and 479, but the empire was barely weakened; it outlived the Athenian empire by a century and shaped Greek politics thereafter mainly through subsidy. It fell to Alexander in three battles, at the Granicus, Issus and Gaugamela. The end is dated to 330 BCE, when Darius III, fleeing east after Gaugamela, was murdered by his own satrap Bessus and Alexander claimed the succession.
